paragraphs: A wireless home camera is deliberately unlike commercial CCTV: white rather than grey, rounded rather than boxed, and small enough to sit on a shelf. The spotlight ring around the lens is the functional giveaway, since it lets the camera record in colour at night rather than in infrared grey.
The mesh is light at 14,614 polygons and 7,473 vertices in quads and tris. The UVs overlap, sensible on a symmetrical moulded body, and the geometry sits in the lens housing and the mount.
At $12 it suits smart home and security product marketing, residential interior and exterior visualisation, e-commerce and retail renders, technology imagery and games. On sale since 2024.

A ratcheting combination spanner has a ring end that turns the fastener one way and slips the other, which means the tool never has to be lifted off. That mechanism sits inside the ring, so the ring is noticeably thicker than on a plain spanner - the identifying feature at a glance.
The mesh is light at 14,716 polygons and 7,360 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, with the geometry in the ring ends, the open jaws and the shank profile.
At $12 it suits workshop and automotive visualisation, tool retail and catalogue renders, trades and DIY material, garage and workbench scenes, and games. On sale since 2023.

The arrow through a wordmark is one of the most copied signage ideas in American roadside design, and it works because it does two things at once: names the business and points at the entrance. The mid century geometry and the palette date it precisely and give a street scene an instant location.

The mesh is light at 11,791 polygons and 12,702 vertices in quads and tris. The UVs overlap, sensible on a symmetrical sign with repeating elements, and the StemCell build means it works in a real-time engine.
At $12 it suits roadside and urban visualisation, retro Americana scenes, film and television set dressing, restaurant and franchise material, and games. On sale since 2025.

A dedicated music player survived the smartphone era by being better at one thing, and the design shows it: a small aluminium body, a physical wheel or buttons that can be worked in a pocket, and a headphone socket given real prominence rather than being removed.

The mesh is minimal at 3,815 polygons and 3,890 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, and ships with 9 texture maps at a mix of sizes up to 4096x4096 carrying the anodised body and the screen.
At $12 it suits consumer electronics visualisation, audio product marketing, e-commerce and retail renders, desk and lifestyle scenes, and games. On sale since 2017.

An early smartwatch is a small screen in a metal case on a conventional strap, and the proportions date it: thick bezels, a squared body and a strap that attaches with ordinary spring bars rather than a proprietary lug. Those details place it precisely in the first wave of the category.
The mesh is light at 10,013 polygons and 10,057 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, and ships with 4 texture maps at 2048x2048 carrying the metal case, the strap and the display.
At $12 it suits wearable technology visualisation, consumer electronics archive material, product and e-commerce renders, desk and lifestyle scenes, and games. On sale since 2016.

An empty jar is a different asset from a full one, and often the more useful of the two: recycling scenes, packaging line renders and label mockups all need the container without contents. Empty, the glass becomes fully transparent and the shape reads through both walls at once.
The mesh is light at 10,272 polygons and 5,140 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, with the lid as a separate body so it can be shown fitted or off.
At $11 it suits packaging and recycling visualisation, label design mockups, food production line scenes, baby care retail renders and games. On sale since 2023.

A wood auger has a screw point at the tip that pulls the bit into the timber, so the operator does not have to push. Behind it a spur scores the circle and a single cutting lip lifts the waste out along a deep flute - a completely different arrangement from a twist drill for metal.
The mesh is minimal at 3,982 polygons and 1,995 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, with the geometry in the flute, the spur and the lead screw.
A second build sits on this page at the same $9. Both suit workshop and joinery visualisation, tool retail and catalogue renders, trades and DIY material, and games. On sale since 2023.

A kerb unit is a precast section with a specific profile: a vertical face to the road, a chamfer at the top and a wider base buried in the bedding. Laid end to end the joints are visible as thin lines, and those joints are what make a street edge read as built rather than extruded.
The mesh is minimal at 1,276 polygons and 640 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, which is exactly right for a modular element repeated the length of a road.
At $9 it suits street and urban visualisation, architectural exteriors, civil infrastructure presentation, driving simulators and games. On sale since 2023.

An earth auger is the same principle as a wood bit at a much larger scale: a lead point, a wide continuous flight and a cutting edge at the bottom. The flight is what lifts spoil out of the hole, and its pitch is what determines how fast the bit clears versus how hard it pulls.
The mesh is minimal at 3,888 polygons and 1,946 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, with the geometry in the helical flight and the cutting head.
At $9 it suits construction and landscaping visualisation, groundworks and fencing scenes, equipment retail and catalogue renders, agricultural material and games. On sale since 2023.

A printed ticket is defined by its perforation: a tear line with a stub on one side, so the same object exists in two states depending on whether it has been used. The card is slightly stiff, it curls at the corners, and the print is usually cheap - all of which distinguishes it from a card.
The mesh is minimal at 1,818 polygons and 1,818 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, with the geometry in the perforation and the slight curl.

At $9 and built to CheckMate specification, it suits event and entertainment visualisation, cinema and venue marketing, editorial and motion graphics, ticketing and app illustration, and games. On sale since 2024.

A nail polish bottle is mostly cap. The brush handle doubles as the closure and is made deliberately large so it can be gripped and turned with polished nails, which is why the proportions look top heavy compared with any other small bottle.
The mesh is minimal at 4,335 polygons and 4,372 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, and ships with 7 texture maps at 1024x1024 carrying the glass, the lacquer and the cap finish.
At $9 it suits cosmetics packaging visualisation, beauty brand and label mockups, retail and e-commerce renders, bathroom and vanity scenes, and games. On sale since 2015.

A small investment bar is minted rather than cast, which gives it sharp square edges, a mirror surface and crisp stamped lettering - completely unlike the rounded, dimpled surface of a poured bullion bar. That difference in finish is what identifies the weight class at a glance.

The mesh is minimal at 2,632 polygons and 2,634 vertices, built entirely from quads with non-overlapping UVs, and ships with 4 texture maps at 4096x4096 carrying the stamped relief and the polished surface.
At $9 it suits financial and investment visualisation, banking and commodities marketing, editorial and news illustration, advertising and print, and games. On sale since 2016.

A payment card is a flat rectangle with a very specific set of features: an embossed or printed number, a chip contact plate, a contactless mark and a magnetic stripe on the reverse. Those elements are standardised globally, which is why a card without them reads as a loyalty tag.
The mesh is minimal at 476 polygons and 240 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, which is exactly right for an object that is essentially a printed plane with a chip on it.
At $9 it suits fintech and banking marketing, payment and e-commerce visualisation, editorial and app illustration, retail checkout scenes, and games. On sale since 2023.

A children's wall light is a shape first and a lamp second: a flat cloud outline in white plastic, lit evenly from behind so it glows as a silhouette rather than casting a beam. That even glow is the design, and it is why the fitting is flat rather than domed.
The mesh is minimal at 4,860 polygons and 2,551 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, with the geometry in the outline and the mounting plate.
At $9 it suits nursery and children's interior visualisation, furniture and homeware retail renders, family and lifestyle imagery, e-commerce material and games. On sale since 2024.
